summary: Hiroshi Deguchi studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1948 to 1953. He held a post at Hokkaido University from circa 1965 to 1987.
Specializing in history, archaeology, and Japanology, Hiroshi Kanaseki studied at Kyoto University from around 1948 to 1953. He later held a post at Tenri University from circa 1987 to 1998.

A Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar, Hiroshi Kanno studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as Director at Soka University and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology, and later became a professor at the International University of Health and Welfare in 2015.

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Hiroshi Kuroda completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University in 1976. He served as an assistant professor at Osaka Gakuin University between 1983 and 1990 and at Osaka Gakuin Junior College in 1988.

An Indology and philosophy scholar, Hiroshi Marui studied at the University of Tokyo, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo in 1992, 1995, and from 1999 to 2018.
Hiroshi Maruyama is a scholar of Indology who held posts as a professor at Osaka University and head of the Ayurveda Research Society in 1987.
Specializing in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Hiroshi Nemoto completed an MA at Hiroshima University. He held posts there as a professor attested between 2015 and 2026.
Hiroshi Tokushige is a Buddhist studies scholar who served at Koyasan University as a commissioned researcher in 2015 and as a specially appointed lecturer in 2026.

A scholar of Indology and religious studies, Hiroshi Yamashita studied at the University of Madras as an international student and served as an associate professor at Tohoku University between 1996 and 1999.
Hirotaka Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism in 2015 and an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.
Hirotomo Teranishi succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 and served as director at Soka University, attested from 2010 to 2012.
A scholar of philosophy, Hiroyuki Kato held posts at Bansho Shirabesho (~1860–1862), Kaisei School (~1869–1877), and the University of Tokyo (~1877–1893).
Linguist Hisanosuke Izui studied at Kyoto University from around 1925 to 1928 and later held a post at Kyoto Sangyo University from circa 1969 to 1976.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Hisao Inagaki earned degrees from Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Ryukoku University, and the University of London. He taught at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as a professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).

Hisao Kanaseki studied at Doshisha University (~1938–1941) and worked in Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Kobe University (~1967–1975), professor emeritus at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1982–1996), and professor at Komazawa University (~1982–1989).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Hisao Takahashi completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, studying under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He held various posts at Taisho University, including lecturer in 1995 and professor from 2004 to 2010.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Hisashi Matsumura studied under Jan Willem de Jong. He held positions at the Australian National University in 1982 and as an assistant professor at Kobe Shinwa University in 1996.

Specializing in Tibetology, history, and archaeology, Hisashi Sato studied at Kyoto University (~1934–1937). He later served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1963–1977), Bukkyo University (~1977–1985), and held professorships at Komazawa and Toyo Universities.

A Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar, Hisataka Ishida studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser in 2011. He was a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University in 2015.

Philosopher Hisatake Kato studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961). He held positions at Yamagata University, the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University, Tottori University of Environmental Studies, and the University of Human Arts and Sciences between 1970 and 2009.
